notes: כָּל־נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם is divided as any (כֹּל), man (אָדָם) and mortally (נֶפֶשׁ); the alternative reads mortally as a free adverb and marks נֶפֶשׁ unrepresented, but rule 2 prefers giving the written word to the morpheme it renders.
אִישׁ takes the recast pronoun he and the casuistic כִּי takes the subordinator that (rule 55); two English words for two morphemes, so rule 30's fusion condition is unmet.
